  COVID-19 PUBLIC PARTICIPATION OPTIONS

  Due to the existing COVID - 19 health emergency and the social distancing measures currently in effect, and pursuant to Assembly Bill 361, please note that members of the public will be allowed to observe and address the City Council Meeting of Tuesday, April 5, 2022, at 2:00 p.m. (or 1:00 p.m. if Closed Session)by call i-n, video, other electronic means, and from the Gladys Waddingham Lecture Hall, as follows:

Written Public Comments: Members of the public may choose to submit comments electronically for consideration by the Inglewood City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Finance Authority/Parking Authority/Joint Powers Authority (Legislative Body) by sending them to the City Clerk/Secretary at athompson@cityofinglewood.org, and Deputy City Clerk at aallen@cityofinglewood.org. Comments received after 8:00 a.m. and prior to the close of the public hearings will be made part of the official public record of the meeting. Inglewood, California
  April 5, 2022

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
  April 5, 2022, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

  Mayor Pro Tem Morales called the City Council into Closed Session at the hour of 1:01
  p.m.
  The City Clerk announced the presence of a quorum as follows:
  Present:  Mayor Pro Tem Morales, Council Members Dotson,
  Padilla, Faulk; and
  Absent:  Mayor Butts.
  City officials and personnel present for closed session were as follows:

  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk
  Ken Campos  City Attorney
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

  MAYOR PRO TEM REMARKS. Mayor Pro Tem Morales announced that CS-1 has
  been pulled from the Agenda.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING CLOSED SESSION ITEM. Mayor Pro Tem
  Morales inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the City
  Council on the Closed Session Item.

  There was no response.

  Mayor Pro Tem Morales recessed the City Council at the hour of 1:02 p.m. for Closed
  Session Item No. CS-2.

  *****************

  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Pro Tem Morales
  called the City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, and Housing
  Authority at the hour of 2:00 p.m.
  The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary announced the
  presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor Pro Tem/Successor Agency Chairman Pro
  Tem/Housing Authority Chairman Pro Tem Morales,
  Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing
  Authority Members Dotson, Padilla, and Faulk; and
  Absent:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman Butts.
  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority officials and personnel present were as
  follows:
  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Louis Atwell  Assistant City Manager/Public Works Director
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority.

  THROUGH MAY 5, 2022, PURSUANT TO ASSEMBLY BILL 361. Staff report

  Absent: Mayor Butts.

  2
 April 5, 2022

 183  PUBLIC HEARING HELD – ORDINANCE NO. 22-07 INTRODUCED – 1)
  ADDING SECTION 2-201 OF ARTICLE 5 OF CHAPTER 2; 2) ADDING
  SECTION 5-112.1 OF ARTICLE 7 OF CHAPTER 5; 3) ADDING SECTION 7-53
  OF ARTICLE 5 OF CHAPTER 7; AND 4) ADDING SECTION 7-79 OF ARTICLE
  7 OF CHAPTER 7. The City Clerk announced the next scheduled matter was a public
  hearing to consider an ordinance of the City of Inglewood 1) Adding Section 2-201 of
  Article 5 (Purchasing) of Chapter 2 (Administration); 2) Adding Section 5-112.1 of
  Article 7 (Water Conservation) of Chapter 5 (Offenses, Miscellaneous); 3) Adding
  Section 7-53 of Article 5 (Solid Waste Code) of Chapter 7 (Sanitation and Health
  Regulations); and 4) Adding Section 7-79 of Article 7 (Construction and Demolition
  Recycling Program) of Chapter 7 (Sanitation and Health Regulations), notice had been
  given in the time, form, and manner as reqired by law, an affidavit was on file, and no
  communications were received.

  Artie Fields, City Manager presented the staff report dated April 5, 2022.

  Angela Williams, Environmental Services Manager gave a brief overview.

  Mayor Pro Tem Morales inquired if there were any persons present that wished to
  address the City Council on this matter.

  Speaker (Name Unknown) spoke in favor of the introduction of Ordinance No. 22-07,
  and thought it would lead the city in a positive direction. She stated that hopefully, this
  would be one of the many environmentally friendly changes that will happen in the
  community. Additionally, she opposed charging the residents for participation in the
  changes or fining them for noncompliance. She believed that state compliance with
  Ordinance No. 22-07 would require more education about the program. Finally, she
  stated that the fees were excessive and would harm the community.

  Mayor Pro Tem Morales closed the public comment portion at the hour of 2:13 p.m.

  It was moved by Mayor Pro Tem Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  further reading be waived. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Faulk, and Mayor Pro Tem Morales;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Mayor Butts.

  Thereupon, Ordinance No. 22-07 entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA 1)
  ADDING SECTION 2-201 OF ARTICLE 5 (PURCHASING) OF CHAPTER 2
  (ADMINISTRATION); 2) ADDING SECTION 5-112.1 OF ARTICLE 5 (SOLID
  WASTE CODE) OF CHAPTER 7 (SANITATION AND HEALTH
  REGULATIONS); 4) AND ADDING SECTION 7-79 OF ARTICLE 7
  (CONSTRUCTION AND DEMOLITION RECYCLING PROGRAM) OF
  CHAPTER 7 (SANITATION AND HEALTH REGULATIONS)

  was introduced by Mayor Pro Tem Morales.

 183 & 301  PUBLIC HEARING CONTINUED – TO CONSIDER THE FOLLOWING
  ACTIONS ASSOCIATED WITH THE INGLEWOOD TRANSIT CONNECTOR
  (ITC) PROJECT. Staff report dated April 5, 2022, was presented to conduct a public
  hearing to consider the following actions associated with the Inglewood Transit
  Connector (ITC) Project:

  1. Adoption of a Resolution Certifying an Environmental Impact Report EA-EIR-2018-
  073 (EA-EIR-2018-073), adopting CEQA Findings of Fact, and adopting Mitigation

  2. Adoption of a Resolution adopting amendments to the Land Use, Safety and
